Hendrix cheat sheet
DIKU GPU cluster · Slurm quick reference
Version: 2025-11-13
Always check wiki for updates

This is a pragmatic cheat sheet for Hendrix. It isn't a full tutorial. The authoritative docs live at diku-dk.github.io/wiki/slurm-cluster . If something here disagrees with the wiki, the wiki wins.

Getting Started

Getting access & help

Access

  • Request role SRV-hendrixgate-users via identity.ku.dk.
  • Mail cluster-access@di.ku.dk with: KU-ID and research section (students: write “student”).

External guests

  • KU employee creates “Science guest” via identity.ku.dk → Manage Identity.
  • Guest requests role SRV-hendrixgate-users and KU employee mails cluster-access@di.ku.dk with guest name + user-id.

Support

  • All cluster issues: cluster-support@di.ku.dk.

Logging in

Prerequisites

  • On KU network (office cable or KU VPN / AnyConnect).

SSH config

Put in ~/.ssh/config (or C:\Users\you\.ssh\config on Windows):

Host hendrix
    HostName hendrixgate
    User <kuid>        # e.g. abc123
    StrictHostKeyChecking no
    CheckHostIP no
    UserKnownHostsFile /dev/null

Connect:

ssh hendrix

You start on a gateway node. Do only light work here (editing, compiling). Heavy experiments must use Slurm.

Cluster Resources

Cluster limits & GPUs

Global limits

  • Max 8 GPUs per user (total across jobs).
  • Default time limit (if not set): 5 hours.
  • Maximum walltime per job: 48 hours.

GPU resources (main gpu partition)

Type Model Count Mem (GB)
H100 Nvidia H100 4 80
A100 Nvidia A100 (40 & 80 GB) 26 40 / 80
A40 Nvidia A40 14 40
titanrtx Titan RTX / Quadro RTX 6000 55 –
titanx Titan X / Xp / V 15 –

General GPU partition name: gpu.

Most useful sbatch / srun options

  • -p, --partition=<name> – queue (usually gpu).
  • --job-name=<name> – job label.
  • --time=HH:MM:SS or D-HH:MM:SS – walltime (≤ 48h).
  • --ntasks=<n> – number of tasks (MPI processes or workers).
  • --cpus-per-task=<n> – CPU cores per task (dataloaders / OpenMP).
  • --mem=<MB|GB> – RAM per node, e.g. --mem=32G.
  • --gres=gpu:<type>:<n> – GPUs, e.g. --gres=gpu:A100:1 or --gres=gpu:2.
  • --array=0-9 – job array indices.

Partitions

  • gpu – main GPU partition (default).
  • cpu – CPU-only partition (if available).
  • Check available partitions: sinfo or scontrol show partition.

Working with Files

Files & data

Copy files

# to Hendrix
scp -r my_file1 my_folder/ hendrix:~/some_dir

# from Hendrix
scp -r hendrix:~/some_dir local_dir/

Mount home with sshfs (Linux/macOS)

sshfs xyz123@hendrix:/home/xyz123 /mnt/hendrix

Windows (SSHFS-Win)

Use "Map network drive" with:

\\sshfs\xyz123@hendrixgate.unicph.domain

ERDA

  • Create account at erda.dk and set up SFTP SSH key.
  • Use sshfs in small mount_erda.sh / unmount_erda.sh scripts and call them at start/end of your Slurm job.

Containers (SIF)

For Singularity/Apptainer images see: slurm-sif page on the Hendrix wiki.

Modules (software)

Use environment modules to load compilers, Python, CUDA, etc.

module avail                 # list modules
module load python/3.9.9     # example
python3 --version

To always load a module, append to ~/.bashrc:

echo "module load python/3.9.9" >> ~/.bashrc

File transfer tips

  • Use rsync for large transfers: rsync -avz file.txt hendrix:~/
  • Compress before transfer: tar czf data.tar.gz data/
  • Check disk quota: quota -s

Job Examples

CPU-only job example

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH -p gpu
#SBATCH --job-name=my_cpu_job
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=4
#SBATCH --time=02:00:00
#SBATCH --mem=8G

echo "Running on $(hostname)"
./my_program arg1 arg2
./post_process.sh

Use CPU-only for preprocessing / analysis. GPU is not required here.

GPU job example

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH -p gpu
#SBATCH --job-name=my_gpu_job
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
#SBATCH --mem=32G
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:A100:1
#SBATCH --time=12:00:00

module load python/3.9.9
module load cuda/...

echo "Node: $(hostname)"
echo "GPUs: $CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"

python train.py --config config.yaml

For two Titan X GPUs, use --gres=gpu:titanx:2.

Job arrays (parameter sweeps)

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=my_array
#SBATCH -p gpu
#SBATCH --array=0-9%3
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=4
#SBATCH --mem=8G
#SBATCH --time=24:00:00

python experiment.py ${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}

10 tasks total (0–9), at most 3 running in parallel. Use the array index to pick seeds or configs.

Slurm Basics

Core Slurm commands

squeue                    # all jobs
squeue -u $USER           # your jobs

sbatch script.sh          # submit batch job
srun --pty bash           # interactive shell on compute node

scancel <jobid>           # cancel job
scancel -u $USER          # cancel ALL your jobs

sacct -j <jobid> \
  -o JobName,State,Elapsed,MaxRss,AllocCPUs

sinfo                     # partition / node status (if enabled)

Monitoring jobs

# Detailed job info
scontrol show job <jobid>

# Job statistics
sacct -j <jobid> --format=JobID,JobName,State,Elapsed,MaxRss,AllocCPUs,ReqMem

# All your recent jobs
sacct -u $USER --starttime=today

# Job efficiency
seff <jobid>              # if available

Useful commands

  • Check node info: scontrol show node <nodename>
  • Job dependencies: --dependency=afterok:<jobid>
  • Email notifications: --mail-type=END,FAIL
  • Working directory: --workdir=/path/to/dir

Best Practices

Memory & utilisation

Estimate memory

Inside a short test job:

/usr/bin/time -v python train.py

Check Maximum resident set size and then request slightly more via --mem.

After job finishes

sacct -j <jobid> \
  -o JobName,MaxRss,State,AllocCPUs

Jobs the scheduler likes

  • Use job arrays for many similar experiments.
  • Prefer shorter jobs (≤ 12–24 h) where possible.
  • Request only the resources you need (GPUs, CPUs, memory, time).
  • Cancel broken or stuck jobs quickly: scancel <jobid>.
  • Do not run heavy jobs on gateway nodes – always go via Slurm.

Quick troubleshooting

  • "Connection closed by …" – your access role might have expired; mail cluster-support@di.ku.dk with the exact error message.
  • Job stuck in queue with (Resources) – waiting for GPUs/CPUs/RAM or higher-priority jobs to finish.
  • Node in drain – usually means jobs will finish then admins reboot or investigate the node.

Performance tips

  • Use --exclusive for full node access (if needed).
  • Set OMP_NUM_THREADS to match --cpus-per-task.
  • Pin GPUs: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 for single GPU.
  • Profile with nvprof or nsys.

Tip: when printing from your browser, enable "Background graphics" for nicer boxes and headings. Remember that Hendrix is a shared resource – good citizenship (reasonable resource requests, cancelling broken jobs) helps everyone.
